text: The Patriots made a significant addition to their offensive line this week by signing OL Matt Pryor from the Arizona Cardinals practice squad, a move that comes at an unfortunate time given that guard Greg Van Roten (thigh) landed on injured reserve Tuesday, continuing the infrastructure damage around quarterback Drake Maye just as New England prepares to travel to Buffalo for a crucial Week 4 AFC East matchup against the undefeated Bills. Maye addressed concerns about his right shoulder on Wednesday, confirming that the physical condition hasn't compromised his throwing ability and instead emphasizing the need for better decision-making as he works to reverse the Patriots' 1-2 start—a struggle that's been painfully evident in New England's last-place offensive performance (9.7 points per game, lowest in the NFL). The Bills, sitting at 3-0, will host the struggling Patriots at the new Highmark Stadium, with Josh Allen looking to put his own occasional sloppy play behind him in what figures to be an early-season divisional reckoning. Off the field, Drake Maye's wife Ann Michael Maye volunteered at Family Food Connections on Tuesday and presented a $100,000 donation from the MayeDay Family Foundation to support the food pantry's mission to families facing food insecurity.
